what: Hovering a photo link makes a 160px circle badge appear in place, growing from 0 in .2s (anchored 120px up-left of the cursor), and it trails the cursor with a .5s (power1.out) delay. On leave it shrinks away in place in .2s. The badge text turns on after it is fully grown and turns off first on exit

options.shift: Distance from cursor to badge top-left (px), default 120
options.look: fade keeps the face size as is and only toggles opacity (in place on leaving), following right away from where it entered. The default is the type that grows from 0
options.pop-ease: Curve for appearing and disappearing, default power1.out
options.center: At 1 the badge center lands on the cursor (shift is not used)
options.from: Rest size — when given, it appears growing from that size and opacity (on entering, it jumps straight to the cursor position) and on leaving shrinks to that size and opacity and disappears. Default grows from 0 (mildsugar .6)
options.out: Fade-out length (sec), same as the default pop (Brand .2)
options.out-ease: Vanishing curve, same as the default pop-ease (power2.in)
options.scroll: If 1, even on scroll it realigns to the last cursor position (even when the board shifts, the badge stays under the cursor) — change-agent

use: In detail…

from.where: index.html project section featured link (.rl-projects__pick) — original front-page inline (.cursor 160px · offset −120 · scale 0→1 .2s · follow gsap default .5s)
index.html Hero ‘Enter the archive’ button (.hero__cursor) — original cursorreveal.js (appear autoAlpha .4s power2.out · follow quickTo .6s power3.out · the button’s exact center is the cursor)
from.options: look: fade; pop: .4; pop-ease: power2.out; lag: .6; ease: power3.out; center: 1

from.where: shared.js MS.stalker (the ‹View› circle on list·article-end stages, the ‹Hi!› circle over the home character — original $s: starts at xPercent/yPercent −50 · scale .6, on enter jumps straight to the cursor position and goes to scale 1·autoAlpha 1 over .3s power2.out, quickTo x·y .4s power3.out, on leave back to .6·0 over .2s power2.in). The original moves a screen-fixed circle with the window mouse while the part moves a circle inside the element — the visible position·values are the same
from.options: center: 1; from: .6; pop: .3; pop-ease: power2.out; out: .2; out-ease: power2.in; lag: .4; ease: power3.out

from.where: index.html uppercase label over card · interview · video thumbnails (.ca-hover) — original card inline script (on every mousemove, left/top are set straight to the cursor position, margin-left 20px, opacity .3s ease on enter and leave, realigned on scroll). The site css overrides the badge background and size so that only text shows instead of a round badge
from.options: look: fade; shift: 0; lag: 0; pop: .3; pop-ease: 0.25,0.1,0.25,1; scroll: 1

from.where: index.js #y-cursor: a navy VIEW circle over menu titles (original .menuSec__btn: from 3px and transparent to 120px and opaque, width/height/opacity .1s ease, its center is the cursor, it follows by half the remaining distance each frame (1 − .5^deltaRatio), and on scroll it adds the scroll amount to the mouse position). The original is a screen-fixed circle that follows the whole window and shrinks to 20px (is-active-min) over description cards. This small type is not in the part.
from.options: center: 1; from: .025; pop: .1; pop-ease: 0.25,0.1,0.25,1; lag: .1; ease: power1.out; scroll: 1; --fx-size: 120px
from.note: The original is a lerp that closes half the distance every frame, so it has no curve name — reaching 98% in six frames (.1s) at 60fps is translated to lag .1 power1.out.

note: Hides the badge on touch. Badge color is the --kf-accent surface with --kf-on-accent text
